context: A node f(k) represents a subproblem of moving k disks. For k greater than 1, first move aside the top k−1 disks, then move the largest disk at the bottom, and finally move the k−1 disks to the destination. Nodes give only subproblem sizes. The source, auxiliary, and destination pegs vary by subproblem and are not labeled.
description: At the top is the original problem f(n), with three children from left to right: f(n−1), f(1), and f(n−1). Each green f(n−1) node on the left or right splits into f(n−2), f(1), and f(n−2). The central teal f(1) needs only a single-disk move and does not split further.

Green boxes are subproblems that need further recursive decomposition. Teal boxes are base cases f(1) that move one disk directly. Ellipses (…) stand for the intervening levels. All nodes at the bottom are teal f(1) boxes. The diagram represents arbitrary n, so counting the teal boxes drawn does not give the move count for a particular n.

frames.explanation: In the code, the central teal f(1) at each split executes move directly, without a separate dfs(1) call. Only the f(1) subproblems reached at the bottoms of the left and right branches, as children of f(2), execute through dfs(1). The diagram therefore shows problem decomposition. Some boxes represent direct moves rather than dfs calls.
frames.title: Tower of Hanoi recursion tree: two smaller tasks and one single-disk move

result: The decomposition gives the following formulas, which are not printed in the figure. Let T(n) count the moves for n ≥ 1. The base case is T(1) = 1, and the recurrence is T(n) = 2T(n−1) + 1. The total is 2 to the power of n minus 1, giving O(2^n) time. The left and right branches run in sequence and reuse stack space after calls return. The longest active chain follows either branch from f(n) → f(n−1) → … → f(1) and contains n dfs stack frames. Counting these frames gives O(n) stack space.
summary: A Tower of Hanoi problem with more than one disk splits into two smaller transfers with one single-disk move between them. Repeat until each task can be performed directly.
title: Tower of Hanoi recursion tree: two smaller tasks and one single-disk move
